orbisterrarum.spawnwait.title: Downloading the map around your spawn
orbisterrarum.spawnwait.text:
Orbis Terrarum is fetching OpenStreetMap data for %s.
%s of %s spawn regions ready · %s s elapsed.
The world will be created automatically as soon as the four regions around the spawn are in.
orbisterrarum.spawnwait.hint: Each region is one request to the public Overpass servers (usually 5–40 s).
orbisterrarum.spawnwait.slow: The public Overpass servers are slow right now (this can take several minutes). Once downloaded, regions are cached on disk and never fetched again.
orbisterrarum.screen.noyacl.title: YetAnotherConfigLib is required
orbisterrarum.screen.noyacl.text: The Orbis Terrarum settings screens need the YetAnotherConfigLib mod (yet_another_config_lib_v3). Install it, or edit config/orbisterrarum/orbisterrarum.json by hand.
orbisterrarum.cat.location.intro: Pick a preset, or type a place name / coordinates and press Look up. Area preview, at the bottom, shows on a map which chunks a pre-generation would make here.
orbisterrarum.map.title: World map
orbisterrarum.map.search.hint: Find a place (Bryggen, Ulriken, an address)
orbisterrarum.map.help: Drag to move, scroll or double-click to zoom, right-click for marks, coordinates and (for operators) teleport. Press N or Esc to close.
orbisterrarum.map.nodata: No map here: this world is not an Orbis Terrarum world, or the server does not run the mod (it tells the map where the world sits on Earth).
orbisterrarum.map.overworld: The map shows the overworld only.
orbisterrarum.map.blocks.tip: The Minecraft world seen from above (as on a map item) over the real map, to find buildings, villages and other structures. Click to change its opacity.
orbisterrarum.map.grey.tip: Grey out the chunks that are not generated yet.
orbisterrarum.map.zoomin: Zoom in to see the Minecraft map and what is generated.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.noworld: This is not an Orbis Terrarum world.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.started: Drawing the Minecraft map of %s regions in the background; /orbis map status shows progress.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.progress: Drawing the Minecraft map: %s of %s regions done.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.idle: The Minecraft map is up to date as far as it has been asked for; /orbis map render draws every region ahead of time.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.done: The Minecraft map is drawn (%s regions).
orbisterrarum.group.spawn.desc: Where players of the new world appear. Off: at the location above (block 0, 0). The map itself stays anchored at the location; only the spawn moves.
orbisterrarum.opt.customSpawn.desc: Players appear at the place below instead of at the location above. Applied once, when the world first starts: the ground there is generated and players stand on top of it (never inside a building). Also set by Look up below, or by right-clicking the Area preview map.
orbisterrarum.opt.spawnSearch.desc: A place name, address or coordinates for the spawn (Bryggen, Bergen / Fløyen / 60.3975, 5.3240). Press Look up.
orbisterrarum.opt.spawnLookup.desc: Finds the place and sets the spawn latitude and longitude, and switches Custom spawn point on.
orbisterrarum.opt.spawnLat.desc: Latitude of the spawn point in degrees (north positive).
orbisterrarum.opt.spawnLon.desc: Longitude of the spawn point in degrees (east positive).
orbisterrarum.opt.exactSpawn.desc: Everyone appears on exactly the spawn block (game rule respawn_radius 0). Off: Minecraft scatters new players up to 10 blocks around it.
orbisterrarum.preview.spawnset: Spawn point set to %s (block %s). It is saved on the Location tab.
orbisterrarum.group.preview.desc: See on a map inside the game which chunks a pre-generation would make around the chosen location, with the chunk and region-file grid and estimates of size and time.
orbisterrarum.opt.previewArea.desc: Empty: the city or municipality the chosen location is in. Or a place name, the same you would give /orbis pregen area (Bergen, Fana, Norway), or a radius in km around the chosen location (5 or 5 km).
orbisterrarum.opt.previewOpen.desc: Opens a map in the game showing the chunks the pre-generation would make, at the location above and the scale on the Scale tab. No need to press Done first. Needs internet for the place lookup and the map.
orbisterrarum.preview.title: Area preview
orbisterrarum.preview.area.hint: Empty = city at the location; or a place, or km
orbisterrarum.preview.go.tip: Look up the area and show the chunks a pre-generation would make (Enter does the same).
orbisterrarum.preview.layer.tip: Map style: street map, satellite photos with place names, or topographic map.
orbisterrarum.preview.lower: Lower ratio: fewer metres per block (1:3 -> 1:2). A bigger, more detailed world with more chunks. Also changes Metres per block on the Scale tab.
orbisterrarum.preview.higher: Higher ratio: more metres per block (1:2 -> 1:3). A smaller world with fewer chunks, a smaller download for friends. Also changes Metres per block on the Scale tab.
orbisterrarum.preview.browser.tip: The same preview as a web page, with more map layers and a place search.
orbisterrarum.preview.finding.here: Finding the area around the chosen location...
orbisterrarum.preview.counting: Found %s (%s km²). Working out its chunks...
orbisterrarum.preview.none: Type an area and press Preview.
orbisterrarum.preview.edge: Part of this lies past the world edge (30 million blocks from spawn): Minecraft cannot generate it. Use more metres per block or a spawn nearer to it.
orbisterrarum.preview.help: Drag to move, scroll or double-click to zoom, right-click to put the spawn point there. Zoom in to see single chunks and region files. A chunk is always 16 x 16 blocks; the scale sets how many metres that is. Ground area counts the block squares covered; crossing times are straight across the widest side. Time assumes about 22 chunks a second.
orbisterrarum.cat.scale.intro: The world spans Y -2032 to 2031. Keep 1 block = 1 m for true 1:1.
orbisterrarum.cat.style.desc: How buildings, roads and nature look.
orbisterrarum.cat.data.sources: Individual imagery and elevation services (URLs, coverage boxes) are edited in config/orbisterrarum/orbisterrarum.json.
orbisterrarum.opt.preset.desc: Well-known places. Selecting one fills in the coordinates below; choose Custom to keep your own.
orbisterrarum.opt.search.desc: For example "Eiffel Tower", "Bergen, Norway" or "48.8584, 2.2945". Press Look up to resolve it (uses OpenStreetMap's Nominatim; needs internet).
orbisterrarum.opt.lookup.desc: Resolves the text above into latitude and longitude and fills them in.
orbisterrarum.opt.originLat.desc: Real-world latitude of block (0, 0). North is positive. Press Enter after typing so the value is taken before you save.
orbisterrarum.opt.originLon.desc: Real-world longitude of block (0, 0). East is positive. Press Enter after typing so the value is taken before you save.
orbisterrarum.opt.worldPreset.desc: Fills in every setting for a kind of world. City 1:1: one block per metre with real buildings, roads, caves and structures. Country map 1:32: one block per 32 m, terrain, water, glaciers, major roads and railways from the map, vanilla-scale towns on the real built-up areas, transverse Mercator projection, coarse elevation tiles; trees, ores, caves, structures and animals stay on for normal survival play -- a whole country in a few gigabytes, ready for Aternos. Import the country's OpenStreetMap extract first (/orbis import) so no Overpass requests are needed.
orbisterrarum.opt.projection.desc: Equirectangular is exact at city scale. Transverse Mercator keeps a whole country's shape and scale right (under 1 % error across Norway). Cannot be changed once the world exists.
orbisterrarum.opt.demZoom.desc: Detail of the Mapterhorn terrain tiles: 15 (~1.2 m per pixel at 60 N, 2.4 m at the equator) for 1:1 worlds, 16 where 1 m lidar exists and you want all of it, 11 for 1:32 country maps, 9-10 for continents. Higher zooms mean more and larger downloads.
orbisterrarum.opt.settlementBuildings.de: For worlds at 8 m per block or coarser, where a real house is smaller than a block: fills every built-up area of the map with vanilla-sized buildings -- houses with pitched roofs on residential land, 3-8 storey blocks on commercial and retail land, halls on industrial land -- so towns and cities are where they really are and as big as they really are. Every storey is lit. No effect on 1:1 worlds.
orbisterrarum.opt.villagerResidents.desc: Households in buildings: a bed on the ground floor (and one upstairs in taller buildings) with a villager per bed. They sleep, wander, flee and breed like a vanilla village. By default they are nitwits who never take a job, so trading stays something you find in real villages. At 1:32, each procedural house gets a bed and a villager.
orbisterrarum.opt.residentJobs.desc: Off (default): residents are nitwits and no workstations are placed, so the only traders are vanilla villages'. On: residents are ordinary villagers and buildings the map names as a business get the matching workstation (bakery -> smoker, library -> lectern, tailor -> loom, smithy -> smithing table, church -> bell, ...), so trades exist where real shops are.
orbisterrarum.opt.buildingSigns.desc: A sign beside every door with the building's real name from the map, or the kind of shop when it has no name. Navigate the city by its street names and shops.
orbisterrarum.opt.furnishInteriors.desc: Furniture by building type: bookshelves and lecterns in libraries and schools, barrels and fish in fishmongers and markets, brewing stands in pharmacies, beds on every floor of hotels, tables and chairs in cafes and restaurants, pews and a bell in churches, shelves in shops and a loot chest in some of them. Entering buildings is worth it.
orbisterrarum.opt.streetLife.desc: Cats in residential streets, sheep and cows on meadows and farmland, a wandering trader on marketplaces, boats moored in marinas, gravestones in cemeteries (dark, so skeletons rise at night) and swings on playgrounds.
orbisterrarum.opt.transitLines.desc: Every railway, tram and light-rail line gets powered rails, connected curves and slopes, and a minecart waiting at each station with the station's name on a sign. Push the cart onto the line and ride the real network.
orbisterrarum.opt.landmarkAdvancements.d: On first start the world gets a datapack with one advancement per real landmark near the origin (peaks, viewpoints, castles, churches, museums, attractions) plus a grand tour for all of them. Delete the world's datapacks/orbis_landmarks folder to regenerate.
orbisterrarum.opt.tunnelLoot.desc: Every 128 m along a road tunnel, an alcove in the wall with a chest worth the fight: 12-24 iron, 2-5 diamonds in one chest out of four, lots of emeralds, gold, copper, lapis, redstone, experience, golden apples, torches, arrows and food, plus an enchanted iron (rarely diamond) tool or armour piece. Tunnels are unlit, so bring a torch.
orbisterrarum.opt.nvdbRoadWidths.desc: In Norway at 1:1 or 1:2, roads without a width in OpenStreetMap take the surveyed carriageway width and lane count of the same road from NVDB (Statens vegvesen, open data, no key). Fetched per region and cached; if the service is unreachable the road class decides, as before.
orbisterrarum.opt.externalPlaces.desc: Merge points of interest imported from Overture Maps (config/orbisterrarum/places, filled by /orbis import-places <file.geojson>) with OpenStreetMap's, so shops, bars, museums and clinics that OSM does not know get furniture and door signs. Places already in OSM under the same name nearby are not doubled.
orbisterrarum.opt.treesFromCanopy.desc: Place every real tree where it stands and as tall as it is, from a canopy height model: the lidar surface model minus the terrain where Kartverket covers, else the Meta / WRI 1 m global canopy map imported into config/orbisterrarum/canopy-cache with tools/canopy_tiles.py. Where a model covers a region no random trees are scattered.
Read each building's roof off the lidar surface model: walls up to the eave, the roof up to the ridge, and flat, gabled or hipped from the height profile across the footprint. Needs the surface model source (Kartverket in Norway); otherwise the building type decides as before.
orbisterrarum.opt.groundClassesFromModel: Ground classes from a segmentation model

Where tools/classify_ground.py has run over the cached aerial imagery (config/orbisterrarum/ground-classes), the model's classes (grass, trees, pavement, bare soil, sand, rock, snow) replace the colour rules for ground the map does not describe.
orbisterrarum.opt.residentsPerChunk.desc: Villagers per chunk on average, spread over the buildings of the chunk (a household is one or two of them). Villager AI is the most expensive thing a server runs: at simulation distance 12 the area around you is 625 chunks, so 0.3 is already about 190 villagers, six large vanilla villages' worth. 0.6 and up stutters on a laptop, on Aternos keep it at 0.2 or lower. Iron golems appear where ten or more live close together.
orbisterrarum.opt.majorRoadsOnly.desc: Only motorways, trunk, primary and secondary roads, railways and runways. For coarse maps, where every street would otherwise merge into one grey blob.
orbisterrarum.opt.metersPerBlock.desc: 1.0 is true 1:1. Larger values shrink the world (2 = half size) and make it generate faster. Press Enter after typing so the value is taken before you save.
orbisterrarum.opt.verticalMode.desc: Minecraft allows 4064 blocks of height and Everest is 8849 m. Relative: exactly 1:1 up to the knee, above it high plateaus sink while peaks keep their full relief (recommended). Compress: only squeeze near the ceiling. Clamp: plain 1:1 cut flat at the top.
orbisterrarum.opt.reliefKneeMeters.desc: Elevation below which the world is exactly 1:1 in Relative mode. 1500 m covers every coast and almost every city.
orbisterrarum.opt.reliefSmoothingKm.desc: Radius of the regional average that high terrain is lowered by. Larger keeps wider areas consistent but squeezes the highest peaks more.
orbisterrarum.opt.seaLevelY.desc: Block Y of real sea level. -1700 leaves 3731 blocks for mountains and 332 for the sea floor. Changing it requires a new world. Press Enter after typing so the value is taken before you save.
orbisterrarum.opt.worldHeight.desc: 0 = fitted to the terrain around the origin when the world is created (a city 1000 m high gets a world about 1800 blocks tall instead of 4064, which makes every chunk about twice as cheap to generate, save and keep in memory). Or a fixed height, a multiple of 16 between 1024 and 4064; 4064 is the full Earth range. The floor (Y -2032) and sea level never move. Fixed once a world exists.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateBuildings.desc: Every OpenStreetMap building, extruded with its real colour, shape and roof.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateRoads.desc: Roads with markings and sidewalks, bridges, tunnels, railways, runways, piers.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateWater.desc: Sea from the coastline, lakes, rivers, canals, pools.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateLandCover.desc: Forests, farmland, parks, beaches, glaciers and other ground types.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateTrees.desc: Trees in forests, parks, gardens and where the aerial imagery shows canopy.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateStreetFurnitur: Street lamps, traffic lights, crossings, benches, fountains, fences, walls, power lines.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateSchematics.des: Hand-built .schem/.nbt models from config/orbisterrarum/schematics placed at their real coordinates.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateBedrock.desc: A bedrock layer at the bottom of the world.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateOres.desc: Coal, iron, copper, gold, redstone, lapis, diamond and emerald veins, placed by depth below the real surface so mining works anywhere on Earth.
orbisterrarum.opt.spawnAnimals.desc: Spawn animals when chunks generate, using vanilla's rules (grass, daylight). Monsters spawn in the dark as usual.
orbisterrarum.opt.vanillaStructures.desc: Mineshafts, strongholds, ancient cities and trial chambers are sunk 100 blocks below the local ground with their vanilla depths kept, so the End is reachable. Villages, temples, outposts, ruined portals, shipwrecks and monuments appear only where the map has no buildings, roads or water.
orbisterrarum.opt.vanillaCaves.desc: Vanilla-style cave tunnels with lava at the bottom, dungeons (mob spawner rooms with chests), amethyst geodes, fossils, water and lava springs and glow lichen, all in the underground band 100 blocks below the local ground. Never opens into streets or under buildings.
orbisterrarum.opt.interiorLights.desc: A sea lantern in every sixth floor block of hollow buildings, so nothing spawns indoors and the mob cap is not used up inside a city.
orbisterrarum.opt.streetLights.desc: Lamp posts every 24 m along lit and urban streets in addition to the mapped ones. Parks, forests and yards stay dark, as in real life.
orbisterrarum.opt.hollowBuildings.desc: Buildings get floors per storey instead of being solid.
orbisterrarum.opt.buildingDoors.desc: A door on the street side of each building.
orbisterrarum.opt.metersPerStorey.desc: Used when only the number of floors is known.
orbisterrarum.opt.roadCenterLineColour.d: Norway and most of Europe: white or yellow; USA: yellow.
orbisterrarum.opt.roadSidewalks.desc: Automatic sidewalks on residential and larger streets.
orbisterrarum.opt.seaFromElevation.desc: Where there is no coastline data, columns below sea level become ocean.
orbisterrarum.opt.treeDensityForest.desc: Trees per column inside forests. 0.045 is one tree per 4.7 × 4.7 m.
orbisterrarum.opt.climateOverride.desc: Auto uses latitude and elevation. Force arid for deserts or humid for jungles where the estimate is wrong.
orbisterrarum.opt.temperatureOffsetC.des: Added to the estimated mean temperature: +3 for Gulf-Stream coasts, -3 for continental interiors.
orbisterrarum.opt.snowTemperatureC.desc: Mean annual temperature below which ground is snow-covered and water frozen.
orbisterrarum.opt.snowAtHighElevation.de: Snow caps above the local snow line.
orbisterrarum.opt.useAerialImagery.desc: Sample orthophotos for roof colours, lawns, pavement, bare soil and tree canopy where OpenStreetMap has no detail.
orbisterrarum.opt.useHighResElevation.de: Also query the GeoTIFF terrain web services in the config (USGS 3DEP, Kartverket) where they have coverage. Normally off: the Mapterhorn tiles already carry the national lidar terrain.
orbisterrarum.opt.useBathymetry.desc: Depths from Open Waters Seascape (GEBCO plus regional surveys) wherever the land data sits at sea level: fjords, harbours and the open sea get their real floor, down to 300 m. Fetched on demand and cached.
orbisterrarum.opt.atlasBuildingHeights.d: Buildings without a height or level tag get their height from the GlobalBuildingAtlas (TUM, every building on Earth, satellite-derived). Fill config/orbisterrarum/heights for your area first with tools/gba_heights.py; nothing changes while it is empty.
orbisterrarum.opt.worldCoverLandCover.de: Where OpenStreetMap has no landuse or natural polygon, take the land cover from ESA WorldCover (10 m, global): forest, shrub, grassland, cropland, built-up, bare ground, snow, wetland. Fetched on demand and cached, no import needed.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryZoom.desc: 18 is 0.6 m per pixel at the equator; 19 is sharper but downloads four times as many tiles.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryRoofColours.des: Untagged buildings get the median orthophoto colour of their roof.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryGroundClassific: Lawn, pavement, soil, sand, rock and snow where OpenStreetMap only has zoning.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryTreeCover.desc: Plant trees where the imagery shows canopy, even outside mapped forests.
orbisterrarum.opt.buildingHeightsFromSur: Where a lidar surface model covers a building without height tags, measure its real height.
orbisterrarum.opt.waitForOsm.desc: Chunks wait until their OpenStreetMap region has downloaded. Off: chunks whose data is not yet there generate as terrain only.
orbisterrarum.opt.prefetchSpawnAtStartup: Download the spawn regions while you are still in the menu so the first world creates instantly.
orbisterrarum.opt.regionPrefetchRadius.d: Rings of 512 m regions kept downloading around each player.
orbisterrarum.opt.regionCacheSize.desc: Decoded regions kept in memory. Each is about 6 MB; lower this on small servers.
orbisterrarum.opt.terrainOnlyBeyondBlock: Chunks farther than this from every player generate at once from elevation alone (no buildings or roads). For distant-horizon mods such as Voxy WorldGen: those chunks are not saved and come back in full detail when you get there. Off waits for map data everywhere.
orbisterrarum.opt.overpassConcurrentRequ: Overpass requests in flight at once. Public servers rate-limit per IP; 4 is safe, 8 only when self-hosting.
orbisterrarum.opt.osmMaxWaitMinutes.desc: How long a chunk waits for its region before generating terrain only.
orbisterrarum.opt.demTileCacheSize.desc: Elevation tiles kept in memory (about 256 KB each).
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryTileCacheSize.d: Orthophoto tiles kept in memory (about 256 KB each).
orbisterrarum.opt.debugLogging.desc: Log every region download and rasterisation.
